articleTitle: Performance analysis of downlink power domain NOMA under fading channels
abstract: The increasing demands of high throughput and capacity in 5G are posing different challenges on the design of multiple access schemes. To meet these challenges, Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is considered as one of the potential candidates. Broadly, NOMA is classified as power-domain and code-domain NOMA. Power-domain NOMA serves multiple users with the same time, frequency and code, but using different power levels. This feature make NOMA capable of increasing spectral efficiency gain over the conventional multiple access schemes. In this paper, an in-depth analysis of downlink power domain NOMA is provided under various fading channels, modulation schemes and channel coding rates. Power domain multiplexing with superposition coding is done at the transmitter side and practical successive interference cancellation (SIC) is used at the receiver side. Performance is analyzed by simulations on the basis of Bit error rate (BER) using AWGN, Rician and Rayleigh channel models for various modulation schemes and code rates. This analysis provides a good foundation for the development of Adaptive Modulation & Coding (AMC) schemes for future NOMA-based 5G systems.

articleTitle: Large lithium-ion battery-powered electric vehicles — From idea to reality
abstract: Lithium-Ion batteries have become the standard for powerful electrical energy supply at mobile applications. Safety is a decisive issue, not only energy per mass or cost. Moving up into energy ranges beyond 100 kWh we have to implement measures against general thermal run-away destruction inherently included in Lithium-ion battery design. In order to gain experience for a hybrid-power locomotive (catenary or battery) a demonstrator was established and successfully tested in 2017. Limited by maximum axle load (21 tons) and the requirement to use as far as possible the existing locomotive (1.6 MW peak, voltage source dc-link, PWM inverter for each of the 4 induction machines; a design of 1980) with its power train, 200 kWh of Lithium-ion batteries could be established. The batteries form 2 strands at 1000 V rated dc voltage each. The battery management system and safety design was based on experience from battery destruction tests of same battery type. Charging of batteries is done over catenary, locomotive main transformer, and existing rectifier by adding a simple resistive current limiter. Battery voltage is directly dc-link voltage for off-catenary operation. The original drive train remains unchanged. In design stage there is a catenary and battery powered large mining truck with over 100 tons payload. Such trucks generally use Diesel engines (about 1000 horse power) and big full-load-capable switchgear and a powerful retarder. The innovation step employs fully electric operation only. Electric energy is used from a special catenary for defined up-slope routes. Hereby, this e.g. 500 kWh Lithium-ion battery (subdivided into e.g. 6 strands) is charged up to the required level. Limited up-slope movement and horizontal driving discharges the batteries. Down-slope driving moves additional charge into the batteries by active braking.

articleTitle: Utilization of modern sensors in autonomous vehicles
abstract: The aim of this work is the development and innovation of localization methods in interior and exterior spaces. In this work, sensors used to locate the position in autonomous vehicle systems are mentioned. Furthermore, this work deals with the fusion of data acquired from different types of sensors as well as their processing.

articleTitle: 3D registration of the point cloud data using ICP algorithm in medical image analysis
abstract: In this article, we are combining an advanced implementation of the popular ICP algorithm using the transformation of 3D invariant properties based on 3D scale-invariant feature transform to register 3D free-form closed surfaces (3D model of the human skull). Unlike point and surface registers, our method based on the ICP algorithm better captures the bulk nature of data such as bone thickness. The proposed ICP algorithm is divided into three main steps: the 3D function extraction, comparison of the Euclidean metric distance and gross alignment and ICP enhancement. The input to our system are biomedical data (CT, MRI). Our proposed method first performs image segmentation and then 3D reconstruction of the human skull. In addition, 3D models for the point clouds (PCs) are created. Finally, the differences between point clouds of 3D models are visualized. We compare the performance of three different algorithms with their accuracy and robustness. The proposed solution is fast and accurate compared to the state of art in the field of reconstruction and registration of medical imagery. We apply our algorithm to study skull deformities. Experiments on skull models demonstrate the efficiency and robustness of our algorithm.

articleTitle: Proposal of a smart water meter for detecting sudden water leakage
abstract: This article deals with a proposal of a smart water meter for monitoring water consumption and for accidental leakage detection. The hardware part of the smart water meter consists of a mini-computer and a pulse water meter. Application logic is then in the hands of the original software that evaluates water consumption patterns. If a water leak is detected, the smart water meter uses a ball valve to close the inlet. The meter also has a self-learning mode that can recommend set limits within the reference period. A separate application interface is designed for communication between the meter and the user. Various computer simulations were used to test and initiate different water consumption scenarios.

articleTitle: Acoustic monitoring and classification of bee swarm activity using MFCC feature extraction and HMM acoustic modeling
abstract: This paper presents a proposed system for acoustic monitoring and classification of bee activity, based on audio modality. Beekeeping is one of the agriculture sectors, where ICT solutions provide great benefit for production and animal welfare. The presented system is a general classifier, which can classify normal and swarm bee activity. The captured audio signal is transformed into mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, which are used to train one state hidden Markov models. The activity classification is carried out in a form of recognition architecture, based on principles applied to speech modality. The acoustic models were trained in a two-stage approach using the open audio data provided by the Open Source Beehives Project. The highest classification accuracy of 80.89% was achieved with the proposed general classification approach.

articleTitle: PAPR reduction of FBMC-OQAM using A-law and Mu-law companding
abstract: Filter bank multicarrier scheme is an efficient multicarrier scheme and candidate waveform for 5G. Similar to OFDM and other multicarrier schemes, FBMC also has high Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR) which leads us to the use of high power amplifiers with high dynamic range. Companding techniques are used to reduce PAPR at the expense of bit error rate (BER) performance degradation. In this paper, a novel usage of A-law and Mu-law companding techniques for PAPR reduction of FBMC-OQAM scheme are proposed. The paper also investigates the tradeoff between PAPR reduction and Bit error rate performance of FBMC-OQAM using A-law and Mu-law companding techniques. Simulation results have shown a significant decrease in PAPR but BER of the system has increased. Both the companding techniques have shown similar results but Mu-law companding has given a slightly better performance than A-law companding in PAPR reduction but BER of A-law companding is better than Mu-law companding.

articleTitle: Inductive coupling system for E-bike wireless charging
abstract: The paper deals with construction design and laboratory measurement of magnetic inductive coupling system suitable for E-bike wireless chargers. It briefly elaborates key design issues relating to the system configuration, material used and given operational properties. The paper also describes fully automatic laboratory equipment for the experimental testing of the system.

articleTitle: Evaluation of SAR in human body model comprising of implanted pacemaker
abstract: The proposed paper deals with simulation and analysis of the mobile phone near-field exposure by evaluation of the specific absorption rate within an anatomical realistic human model comprising of implanted pacemaker model. The research was carried out using electromagnetic modeling based on the Finite Integration method. The main objective was to compare levels of absorbed electromagnetic energy as function of antenna distance and mobile phone carrier frequency. The results have shown that averaged SAR induced by the antenna model operating on GSM standard were approx. three times higher than in the case of UMTS standard. However, dosimetric limits for public exposure were not exceed in all considered scenarios.

articleTitle: Direct-torque control system design using maximum torque per ampere method for interior permanent magnet synchronous motors
abstract: The paper proposes a method for controlling interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (IPMSM) drives, that combines Direct-Torque control (DTC) and Maximum Torque Per Ampere (MTPA) in a synchronously rotating (d-q) frame. It has been proven that the increase of electromagnetic torque is proportional to the increase of angle between rotor and stator flux linkages. The use of the DTC method for controlling IPMSM shows a quick and robust response with torque and flux ripples. Combined with MPTA the efficiency of the system is increased as there is no need for prior estimation of flux. Also, speed control loop with PI controller is also introduced to the system for speed regulation. Here, we introduce a simple MTPA-based DTC scheme with speed control with satisfied performance. The feasibility of the system is confirmed by Simulink model, the results of which are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Inverse kinematics using transposition method for robotic arm
abstract: Forward and inverse kinematics of the DOBOT manipulator is presented in this paper. Forward kinematics refers to the use of the kinematic equations of a robot to compute the position of the end-effector from specified values for the joint parameters. For forward kinematics we used analytical solution and we made Jacobi matrix by derivate kinematics equations. Inverse kinematics makes use of the kinematics equations to determine the joint parameters that provide a desired position for the robot's end-effector. The inversion of Jacobi matrix was used for numerical solution of the inverse kinematics task. Simulation was created in Matlab environment using SimMechanics toolbox and in second case by described numerical solution.

articleTitle: Avalanche forecasting using neural network
abstract: In this paper avalanche forecasting and usage of snow and weather data in artificial system, that is able to do avalanche forecasting, is shortly described. These weather data are acquired from Automatic weather stations. In this paper Fast Artificial Neural Network for avalanche forecasting system with artificial intelligence is used. In section II. variables for neural network input are described by their functions. At the end of this paper the different architectures of neural network are tested and their results are evaluated. Testing data contains data from AWS from winter 2009/2010 to winter 2016/2017.

articleTitle: The use of e-learning at foreign language practical lessons in a technical university
abstract: This electronic document deals with the use of E-learning at foreign language practical lessons in a technical university, the work experience of Foreign Languages Chair of Ryaz an State Radio Engineering University.

articleTitle: PI anti-windup speed control of permanent magnet synchronous motor based on feedforward compensation
abstract: This paper designs simulation model of PI anti-windup speed controller based on a simple set-point weighting for the interior permanent-magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM). Firstly, a mathematical model of IPMSM drive system utilized in the simulation is introduced. Also, the maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) control suitable for IPMSM was employed. This controller is simple for implementation in practice and it has advantages over a conventional PI controller. The proposed anti-windup PI controller demonstrates better dynamic step changes response in speed in terms of overshoots, improved settling time, and improved robustness to parameter variations in comparison with conventional PI. The performance of proposed PI anti-windup controller with set-point weighting was compared with the conventional PI.

articleTitle: The analyse of the various methods for location of Data Matrix codes in images
abstract: Data Matrix codes belong to the group of 2-D bar codes, which are widely used in marking the products in storing, production, distribution and sales processes. Their compact matrix structure enables to store big amount of information in a very small area compared to conventional 1-D bar codes. In following paper we compare several methods for detection of Data Matrix codes in images. When locating the position of the code we start from typical bordering of Data Matrix code - which forms “L” so called Finder Pattern and to it the parallel dotting so called Timing Pattern. On the first stage we try to locate Finder Pattern using the edge detection or adaptive thresholding, then continuing with connecting the points into the continuous regions, we are searching for the regions, which could represent the Finder Pattern. On the second stage we verify Timing Pattern where the number of crossing between the background and foreground must be even.

articleTitle: Evaluation of packet forwarding approaches for emergency vehicle warning application in VANETs
abstract: Cooperative Intelligent Transportation Systems (CITS) based on a communication between vehicles and intelligent roadside infrastructure can be of a great benefit regarding road safety, traffic congestion and environmental impact of the transport. One of their key technologies are the Vehicular Ad hoc Networks. Due to the high mobility of the nodes that form the network, some protocol data unit forwarding approaches cannot achieve acceptable results under certain conditions. In this paper we evaluated the performance of L2 broadcasting and L3 routing using AODV and GPSR routing protocols to forward messages of an emergency vehicle approach warning application for connected and autonomous vehicles under specific road traffic conditions in the city of Zilina. To run the simulations, we used the highly realistic simulation stack comprising of OMNeT++ network simulator coupled with SUMO traffic simulator by Veins simulation framework.

articleTitle: Current controller with slope compensation for a switched reluctance motor
abstract: This paper describes development of a current controller for a Switched Reluctance Drive used in a traction application. Motor parameters are measured and evaluated. A suitable simple and high dynamic controller is proposed, with current slope compensation to mitigate over regulation. Finally the proposed regulator is compared with other alternatives.

articleTitle: HW issues of current sensing by DC-link shunt resistor
abstract: This paper deals with issues and challenges of current sensing using DC-link shunt resistor in three-phase power inverter motor control applications. Main parameters of shunt resistors relevant to the DC-link current sensing are discussed. Main factors influencing the accuracy are described, including the shape of the footprint and soldering. An example of a sensing circuit is introduced, discussing the key parameters and challenges needed to be dealt with in terms of the accuracy of the measurement and mainly the proper operation of the sensing circuit in the whole range of operation.

articleTitle: AC/AC powertrain control under different HEV supply network
abstract: The paper deals with direct AC-AC propulsion system using [3×5] matrix converter and five-phase traction induction motor (IM) for the hybrid electric vehicle (HEV). Using the direct AC-AC system, in comparison to classical rectifier-inverter with DC link, features smaller on-state semiconductor switches losses at full load operation and consequently higher efficiency of the powertrain of the vehicle. The major advantage of using a five-phase machine instead of three-phase one is smaller torque pulsation and better fault tolerance after the loss of one phase of feeding source. There are presented comparative analyses of AC/AC powertrain under different HEV supply network: as a fixed voltage source, a soft voltage source with input LC filter, and using the electromechanical model of ICE engine and PMSG generator. Modeling and simulation are done using Matlab-Simulink environment, and simulation experiments are given in the paper.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of low-cost and low-energy sensor for wireless sensor networks
abstract: The proposed article introduces a design of low-cost and low-energy wireless sensor network comprising of one central node and multiple peripheral sensor nodes. As a wireless technology, the nRF24L01+ transceivers modules operating in unlicensed 2.4 GHz band are used. The main effort is focused on the optimal selection of wireless communication parameter to ensure reliability and data transmission range between central and sensor node. Furthermore, a design and implementation of wireless sensor node to detect windows state is discussed. A conducted series of experiments to evaluate the power efficiency and communication reliability have revealed that the proposed wireless sensor network is suitable for Smart Home application where these parameters are crucial. The transmission power of developed sensor node is approx. 1 mW, thus operating in standby mode up to 232 days while driven by a single coin battery.

articleTitle: Control strategy for parallel-connected three-phase inverters
abstract: In this paper, a control strategy for parallel connected three-phase voltage source inverters is presented. The control strategy is based on the droop control method, which does not require interconnection and communication between individual inverters of parallel connected system. In each of the parallel connected inverters, the inner control structure in Direct-Quadrature (DQ) rotating frame is used. The outer control loop ensures appropriate loads sharing. The whole control system is described, and dynamic and static behavior is verified by simulations.

articleTitle: Current harmonics compensation in single-phase grid-connected inverter
abstract: This paper presents a power control of a single-phase voltage source inverter for grid-connected photovoltaic system. The proposed method is based on vector control of power by decoupling control of the active and reactive current components to feed the active power to the grid. The aim of this research is to control power at grid, to alternate current power conversion into the grid, and to decrease phase current distortion of VSI. To improvement of the current distortion is used current control scheme with compensation 3rd and 5th harmonic components. In the last two chapter are shown the simulation and experimental results of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Use LLVM for optimization of parallel execution of program code on the certain configuration
abstract: Automating of parallelization requires the analysis of program code from the point of view of semantic relations between operations. At the same time, up-to-date tools for automation of parallelization usually have a number of restrictions related to binding the parallelization system to the language on which the source code is written. The other restrictions appear from requirement to indicate the blocks in program code should be implemented in parallel or even make some “modifications” of the code in manual mode. The LLVM system provides manifold possibilities for automation of code analysis and optimization for its subsequent parallel execution. The article discusses the approach to parallelization of sequential program code by using LLVM for code analysis and its presentation in the form of semantic Petri-Markov nets.

articleTitle: Subjective and objective evaluation of spatial and temporal information of video content
abstract: This paper deals with a video content classification based on spatial and temporal information. The main goal of the paper is to find out whether the non-expert test subjects are able to correctly recognize the spatial and temporal information and how precise is the corresponding parameterization of video content based on these two attributes. Moreover, how well do the objective values provided by the tool deployed in this experiment correlate with the subjective ones. The subjective measurement has shown that the non-expert test subjects are able to correctly recognize the spatial and temporal information only for the extreme scenes in terms of the spatial and temporal information but have experienced some problems when it comes to a more granular classification. When it comes to the objective assessment, the SI and TI values provided by the tool used in this experiment correlate quite well with the subjective data obtained from the basic test for the spatial information.

articleTitle: Wheeled mobile robot in structured environment
abstract: Industrial mobile robots are special kinds of industrial robot dedicated to handling or working with object during the locomotion. Paper deals with simulation of wheeled mobile robot in structured environment. Motion of undercarriage and manipulator are as contemporary motions. The simulation is used for identification of required actuator torque for every joint of mechanism.

articleTitle: Overview of technology, problems and comparison of high speed synchronous reluctance machines
abstract: This article is focused on review of applications with high speed synchronous reluctance machines. It deals with design, main problems, drives, controlling and challenges in new branch of this electrical machines. The examples and comparison of solution are presented. The problems with construction and some problematic detail are described.

articleTitle: Experimental study of ball on plate platform
abstract: This paper is extension of article SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL STUDY OF BALL POSITION CONTROL AT BIAXIAL PLATFORM USING STATE SPACE APPROACH, which came out in number 1/2018 of journal Komunikácie (Communications). This extension is focused on other control techniques, which have wider bandwidth. This paper presents design of state space observer with state space feedback, which is extended by compensator to achieve better dynamic properties of control structure. Another presented control technique is sliding mode control, which is more robust and has also wider bandwidth. Control structures are designed for stabilization of the ball's position on a plate and for capability of trajectory tracking. All techniques are designed, practically verified and compared. Pole placement method was used for calculating of the parameters of the proposed control structures.

articleTitle: The influence of nanoparticles in the epoxy resin on dielectric parameters and partial discharges
abstract: The influence of nanoparticles (SÍO2, TÍO2, ZnO) in epoxy resin on the changes of the complex permittivity and the time to breakdown have been measured. Frequency dependences of the real and imaginary parts of complex permittivity were measured within the frequency ranges from 1 mHz to 2 MHz by a capacitance method. The 1 wt.% nanoparticles caused the decrease of the complex permittivity. At the study of the influence of temperature on the imaginary permittivity, a-polarization was observed. The characteristics of internal partial discharges in the cavity of the epoxy resin and its mixtures with nanoparticles by the Galvanic method have been measured, too. The partial discharge measurements were performed with the help of Phase Resolved Partial Discharge Analyzer. Nanoparticles significantly affected on the time of breakdown. The filler SiO2 had positive and fillers TiO2 and ZnO had a negative influence on time to breakdown.

articleTitle: RGB-D imaging used for OSAS diagnostics
abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSAS) is a respiratory disorder increasing its prevalence with significant consequences for pediatric patients. The accurate diagnostics of this syndrome is now very time consuming procedure consisting mainly of video polysomnography in sleep laboratory. Due to absence of sleep laboratories (pediatric sleep laboratory is only at Clinic of Children and Adolescents in Martin), the authors of this pilot study focus on using RGB-D depth imaging for supporting diagnostics of OSAS. Based on questionnaire of pediatric specialists from Rome (Italy) specific dentofacial (craniofacial) features measured on head strongly correlate with OSAS occurrence and patients for more accurate diagnostics can be selected during the primary examination. Authors bring a comparison of some RGB-D sensors and measurements for selected dentofacial features to create supporting, non-invasive, automated and fast method for preliminary confirmation of OSAS.

articleTitle: Towards the development of a wearable temperature sensor based on a ferroelectric capacitor
abstract: Response of a ferroelectric capacitor to static temperature (~22 to 90°C) is presented. The sensor is based on ferroelectric ceramic lead zirconate titanate (PZT). The PZT sensor is a cheap, commercially available element used to provide a proof of concept for the initial investigation into using ferroelectric materials for the monitoring of static temperature. The capacitor response to temperature was measured using PZT capacitance changes recorded at 1 kHz. The capacitance was measured after the temperature had stabilised. We have found that the PZT capacitor responds linearly as a function of applied temperature, with a sensitivity ~53 pF/°C. Furthermore, to provide some initial electronics capable of measuring sensor capacitance in real time, the PZT element was attached to an Arduino Uno platform. Again, the sensor continues to respond linearly to temperature with a sensitivity of 146 pF/°C. The system developed paves the way for further work to be done on using ferroelectric materials for the monitoring of static temperature changes, for applications such as human body temperature measurement using a textile-based smart-shirt setup.

articleTitle: Comparison of detection abilities between fluxgate and GMR magnetometer in inverse ECT of deep lying cracks
abstract: This article deals with the inverse problem solution in nondestructive evaluation of conductive materials. The eddy current inspection is used for the measurements and the MATLAB software is used for post-processing of the gained signals. Geometry parameters of the inspected cracks are analyzed by use of wavelet transform and artificial neural network. The gained results are presented and discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Analysis of winding fault in electric machines by frequency method
abstract: Article presents experimental analyses of faults in winding of transformers and rotating electric machines. The first part of article deals with the possibilities of diagnostics for windings electrical machines. The second part of article deals use of frequency method SFRA (Sweep Frequency Response Analysis) for analyse winding fault. Finally, the article presents experimental measurements of diagnostics for analysis of the windings in distribution transformer and rotating electric machine. On both of the investigated machines is analyzed internal winding fault.

articleTitle: Energy hub — The sollution for overcomming negative impacts of massive electromobility — Case study
abstract: In this paper, the brief analysis of the circuit solution of power electronic system integrated within DC-micro grid system of the intelligent hub was realized. The main reason for this approach is the necessity to identify possibilities which may enable to boost massive electromobility within upcoming years. Several proposals for the intelligent power hub are considered, while attention is given for the solution of the power electronic systems. Almost these parts of whole system present the most challenging issue when overcoming of negative disturbances related to the massive electromobility is considered.

articleTitle: Investigation of structural changes in liquid crystal doped with superionic nanoparticles
abstract: Using both acoustic and optical techniques in liquid crystals doped with superionic compounds Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>PSI<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>/CU<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sub>PS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub> in 50:50 ratio dispersed in liquid crystal host, where structural changes on applied electric field are observed. The investigation methods involve measurements of acoustic attenuation of surface acoustic waves (SAW) and electro-optical response measurements using linearly polarized laser beam (532 nm) propagating through the sample. Both methods examine the system response on applied electric field for its increasing/decreasing application as well as change after jump change. Results obtained from these two methods are compared to show effectivity of these measurements, suspension stability and switching time.

articleTitle: Application diagnostic of distributed control system with safety PLC
abstract: Nowadays almost all commercially available control systems, allow modularity of architecture. It is also similar for control systems based on safety PLC (Programmable Logic Controllers) intended for realization of safety functions. With more possibilities of modularity, we have more choices, how to realize safety functions. Diagnostics is also necessary to achieve the required safety integrity level (SIL) of safety functions. The way how to realize diagnostics for distributed control system can be different than realization of diagnostics for centralized control system. This paper addresses the analysis of the influence of diagnostics in distributed control system on the safety integrity level of realized safety functions.

articleTitle: Start — Up power supply for automotive applications
abstract: This article introduces the analysis of car start-up power supply with novel main circuit design combining perspective circuit and component solutions. The application area is automotive industry and car service companies. This design combines the use of switched power converter with a lithium-titanate accumulator (LTO) and supercapacitor (EDLC) as energy storage elements. The main topology of the power supply is realized as full-bridge resonant LLC switched converter in connection with two-phase interleaved PFC circuit, which are not presented here. The main aim of the presented paper is description and verification of control circuitry for auxiliary storage elements. Initially, main circuit components are listed. Consequently, the control scheme is shown and designed within OrCAD PSpice simulation tool. The proposed control scheme is consequently verified together with the model of proposed power supply. Working characteristics of the designed converter are modified in order to achieve requested parameters and highest possible efficiency. [1], [3].

articleTitle: Complete elecric power steering system real-time model in the loop simulator
abstract: The paper presents a complete mechanical and electrical chain of an electric power steering (EPS) system analyzed on a real-time model in the loop (RTMiL) test platform based on usage of field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). Based on an analytical model, the mechanical, electrical and control assemblies of the entire system were programmed into two FPGAs using National Instruments LabVIEW FPGA program. One FPGA was handling the control unit of the electrical machine and of the steering mechanism, while the second one was handling the modelling of the permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) engaged in the study and the model of the mechanical chain. The two FPGAs were connected in order to mimic a real test-bench. On analog lines, the currents from the PMSM model were sent to the field oriented control (FOC) handling FPGA, on 8 bit digital lines the rotor position was delivered to the same FPGA. The control handling FPGA delivers to the PMSM and steering mechanics handling FPGA PWM signals using 3 digital lines. Hence, the two FPGAs practically have no knowledge one over the other that these are running models instead of a real electronic control unit (ECU) or the real hardware steering chain.

articleTitle: Common frequency extraction for bandpass sampling based frequency de-hopper
abstract: In Complex EW environment, modern frequency hop radars tend to change their frequencies from pulse to pulse, making their blind estimation a challenging task. A band pass sampling based frequency estimation approach was proposed in [1] which relies on generating three frequency image vectors and searching their common image through correlation. In this paper, we have analyzed different search algorithms rather than simple correlation for extraction of common frequency image among multiple frequency vectors. An efficient algorithm with minimal time complexity is proposed after performance comparison of linear, binary, merge and interpolation search algorithms. It is shown that the time complexity is highly dependent upon the selection of sampling frequencies and the lengths of frequency image vectors through simulations of different possible scenarios.

articleTitle: Dual interleaved power factor correction for welding inverter
abstract: Main aim of this article is proposal for design approach, consequent simulation and practical implementation of single-phase active rectifier (PFC) designed for a welding inverter with output power of 4kW and output voltage of 400V. The efficiency of PFC should be greater than 95%, and the power factor (PF) at full power load should be more than 98%. Proposed PFC should further comply with international standard IEC 61000-3-2 Class B (Non-Professional Welding Equipment) which is relevant for electromagnetic compatibility regulations by conduction and sets the upper limit of higher harmonic input current. Practical experiments shows, that the design approach is correct and proposed procedure has given required results.

articleTitle: Advanced superconducting tapes for high voltage fault current limiters
abstract: Superconducting fault current limiters based on high temperature superconducting coated conductors are novel devices which enables further development of the electricity network. In this contribution analyse properties of advanced superconducting tapes with modified architecture to withstand higher electric fields and thus higher heat generation during limiting period. We have shown that additional heat capacity layer, made of hasteloy, reduces maximum temperature of superconductor despite of enhanced heat generation resulting from lower resistance of the modified tape.

articleTitle: Modelling of the diagnostics influence on safety integrity of safety function
abstract: The paper is dedicated to modelling the diagnostics influence on the hardware safety integrity of safety function implemented by safety relevant electronic system. In the paper, by means of homogenous Markov chains, is analysed the influence of different forms of diagnostics and its basic parameters - diagnostic coverage coefficient and failure detection and negation time, on the hardware safety integrity of safety function.

articleTitle: The main capabilities and solutions for different types of the image sensors
abstract: The paper deals understanding terminology and problematic for image sensors how are CCD and CMOS and differences between them or what does mean rolling shutter, global shutter etc. This paper use also as a first step for research image sensor with cooperation ON Semiconductor.

articleTitle: Comparison of DC conductivity of the insulating oil and moisturized electrical pressboard impregnated with insulating oil
abstract: In the paper presents compares the DC conductivity of the insulating oil manufactured by Nynas and electrical pressboard Pucaro companies impregnated with the same insulating oil with different moisture contents. The study of conductivity for both materials were made for the measuring temperature in the range of 20 °C to 80 °C and measuring voltages in the range from 20 V to 1000 V. In the Arrhenius plots for both materials were been performed linear approximations of experimental results. On the basis of Arrhenius plots for the oil and the sample for the pressboard, for all measuring voltages, the value of the activation energy value of the DC conductivity and the determination coefficient R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> was determined. The value of the determination coefficient close to one indicates the high accuracy of conductivity measurements. Comparing the activation energy value of the DC conductivity for insulating oil and pressboard impregnated with the same oil, it can be concluded that the conduction in pressboard is not caused by the presence of oil in the solid component of the paper-oil insulation.

articleTitle: Synthesis of a robust control algorithm for a robot positioning
abstract: This contribution presents an original reaching law approach to the continuous approximation of the discontinuous (relay) element in robust variable structure motion control systems (VSC). The suggested approximation is implemented to get a continuous method of the actuating variable generation, to prevent the chattering (i.e. the parasitic low frequency oscillation) and to preserve the desired control performance in real motion systems like robotic manipulators, mobile robots and other MIMO or SISO mechatronic systems. Numeric simulation shows the feasibility of the proposed control algorithm.

articleTitle: Optimization of the distribution network operation based on data from distribution substations
abstract: The paper is dealing with the current trends in the implementation of a Smart Grids concept in a power distribution system. An emphasis is put on the information acquisition from distribution substations, as they will very soon become important communication nodes providing several types of data (e.g. alarms, station control data, real time monitoring, energy measurements, power quality measurement, demand profiles, etc.), which can be successfully used in the optimization of distribution system operation. Results of such optimization, based on a real measured data and SOMA based optimization algorithm, are provided for a test distribution network.

articleTitle: Calculation of the output value distribution of the GERT network with exponentially and evenly distributed random values
abstract: A brief overview of the applications of GERT networks for the modeling of industrial systems is provided. System characteristics analysis is performed using equivalent simplifying transformations of the GERT network structure. Algorithms with polynomial computational complexity are suggested. The distribution density of the continuous output value of the GERT network is calculated with interpolation of the characteristic function of the network. Ways to maintain an acceptable error rate of an inversion formula are described. This method is used if the GERT network has paths from the entrance to the exit which include only arcs with exponential and even distributions. The desired distribution is based on the residue theory with simple poles and recoverable special points in the integration contour. The decomposition of the integral function to a Laurent series in the vicinity of an infinitely remote point is used. An example of calculation of the time allocation density of the production process is given.

articleTitle: Determination of the big mammals migration corridors in the particular areas using remotely-operating intelligent camera system
abstract: Large mammals free movement through the large areas is fundamental element of the healthy mammals ecosystem. The migrations keep the balance between animal populations, maintain sufficient genetic diversity or prevent the temporary lack of food. With the growing rate of transportation, urbanization and industrialization across the all countries, the barriers in the countrysides are created. Because of these barriers, the natural migration corridors of big mammals are endangered. Preserve the land connectivity is fundamental step for nature conservation and for healthy mammals ecosystem. To achieve this objective, we proposed a camera-based remotely operating intelligent system to identify the migration corridors. The system consists of one master device and more slave devices. The slave devices are deployed in the harsh environment of the countrysides and they use two camera devices to detect and track mammals across their surveillance zone. The information about mammals movement, movement trajectory and time in the scene are send to the master and stored in the database. The system uses the algorithm of computer vision to automatically classify appropriate animal species for moving mammals. The master collect data from all slave devices in the designated area and then the migration corridors for individual mammals species are created.

articleTitle: Reverse validation of a programmed robot trajectory based on INS
abstract: The paper deals with Implementation of inertial navigational system in industrial robot control. The goal of this paper is the verification of the possibility of trajectory control and correction (reverse validation) of a mobile robot, which is based on an implemented inertial navigation system even in situations, when the inertial navigation system is the only trajectory control device. Adjustments to the trajectory of mobile robot are dependent on positional data of the robot, obtained via sensors located on the industrial robot. The mentioned IMU data were processed in real-time with different ways to gather positional information about the movement of the device. An x-IMU was proposed and used as the inertial navigation system an. It was located at the End Point of the robot's effector (EE point). To control the convergence rate, optimized Madgwick AHRS algorithm has been proposed.

articleTitle: Concept of control system for optimal switching of phase shifting transformers
abstract: Paper presents an innovative concept for automatic selection of an optimal tap of the phase shifting transformer (PST) before its switching-on. The purpose of the system is to enable the switching-on of the PST without sudden changes in power network operating conditions. For the investigation of the underlying phenomena during switching, a test power network containing the accurate dynamic model of the PST was developed. The investigations were performed for different scenarios of changes in the power network parameters and control options of the PST. This allowed determining the desired functionality and structure of the automation system for selecting an optimal tap of the PST before its switching-on. The developed automation system is based on synchronous measurements, and this represents a novel implementation of such measurements. Verification simulation studies indicate that the proposed concept achieves the stated objectives. It is expected that the practical application of this automation system can resolve the transient overcurrent in the adjoining network components arising from PST switching. Overall this will enable significant minimization of negative effects of PST switching-on the power network operating conditions.

articleTitle: Photomultiplier tube amplitude improvement using collection time information
abstract: The main goal is to present method to improve amplitude information acquired by photomultiplier tube using collection time. Two PMT85 photomultiplier tubes are positioned opposite to each other at the outside cylindrical surface of the thin scintillator. After amplitude recalculation obtained value will serve as true one for detector calibration. Direct relation between LED flash position and collection time is observed.

articleTitle: Mathematical model of non-linear RFID reader — Transponder system
abstract: This paper deals with the describing and modeling of inductively coupled radio frequency identification (RFID) system consisting of the transponder and reader basic circuitry where the transponder is considered as a system with non-linear current-voltage characteristic. This non-linear characteristic has significant influence on the signals transferred from the transponder to the reader so the comparison of linear and nonlinear model of the transponder is performed. Moreover the simple measurement method of the non-linear current-voltage characteristic of the RFID transponder chip EM4100 and its approximation by mathematical functions is described.

articleTitle: Low frequency electromagnetic field treatment of yeast cells targeting specific ion channels
abstract: The presented article discusses the ion parametric resonance theory, especially the modified parametric magnetic resonance version published by V.V. Lednev and attempts to verify the validity thereof in view of specific ion channels. To this end, several experiments with IPR-compliant EM field parameters for specific ions (Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+, Mg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+, K+) have been conducted on Saccharomyces Cerevisiae (yeast) strands, as well as non-IPR compliant (chosen randomly but within the expected bioactive ranges) combinations. Statistical analysis of the calculated exposed/control colony forming unit ratios has confirmed a statistically significant effect of the applied electromagnetic field for specific ion types, whereas the randomly chosen parameters have not. The results present a good basis for further research in this area with the ultimate aim of pin-pointing the exact receptors responsible for the observed changes in proliferative response.

articleTitle: Research and practical realization of RF microstrip band-stop filter using transmission line theory
abstract: In this paper, the analyzation and practical realization of RF microstrip band-stop filter using transmission line theory is presented. A simple measurement method has been used for determination of relative permittivity of dielectric substrate at given frequency band. The S-parameters of realized band-stop filter structure has been compared with S-parameters obtained from MATLAB and S-parameters obtained from EM simulator. The results are in good agreement.

articleTitle: Enhanced sensitivity of polydimethylsiloxane Fabry-Perot interferometer temperature sensor
abstract: A polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) Fabry-Perot interferometer placed at the end of single-mode optical fiber is proposed and demonstrated experimentally. The temperature sensitivity of the interferometer 2.5 nm /°C in the range 28 °C to 35 °C was achieved. To enhance the sensitivity of the temperature sensor another interferometer (in Mach-Zehnder configuration) was used. In this case the sensitivity is enhanced by Vernier effect. The temperature sensitivity was enhanced to 14.8 nm/°C what is almost 6 times higher. Interesting attribute of such configuration is possibility to change free spectral range (FSR) of the second interferometer due to optical path difference settings. So, it is possible to change the sensitivity of the sensor.

articleTitle: Structural numerical and experimental comparison of an in-wheel motor dedicated for electric scooter application
abstract: This paper describes a structural behavior of a permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM), used to propel an in-wheel motor, namely an electric scooter. Since the rotor and the stator core are under electromagnetic force influence, both parts of the machine are separately analyzed. This analysis is carried out in order to observe the mode shapes of the PMSMS, produced by radial forces. These mode shapes represent, in part, the image of the vibration and noise produced by the PMSM - which is the authors' intention to evaluate finally. The analysis is carried out, firstly, by using LMS Virtual. Lab software; here, based on an appropriate discretization one can investigate, on a larger frequency range, the mode shapes of the structure. Next, the experimental mode shapes are evaluated by performing the so called impact testing. The comparison of the numerical and experimental results depicts the consistency of the work.

articleTitle: Expert system of multi-criterion fuzzy management of computing resources
abstract: We suggests a new methodology of smart management of computing resources based on set-theoretic explicit and implicit clustering. We have analyzed production, frame and semantic nets modeling of knowledge on the basis of explicit clustering, and for fuzzy structures, through implicit clustering. A set of modeling software has been developed for multi-criterion fuzzy management of selection according to various technical specifications: system performance, the number of computing modules, microprogram memory capacity, etc.

Author Keywords: frame and semantic nets modeling of knowledge

articleTitle: Comparison of analog and discrete energy detectors of the deterministic radio signals of unknown form
abstract: We carry out the efficiency comparison of analog and discrete energy detectors. Unlike the approach presented in the popular studies, we deal with the case of nonoptimal reception. As a useful signal, the determined narrow-band signal is considered for which the bandwidth is known, while both the form and some other parameters remain unknown. For this case, we find the distribution of decision statistics for the discrete energy detector and prove that in energy of response discrete detector is almost equivalent to the analog one. Thus, here we see no loss in detection quality due to the discretization.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic torque ripple calculation of a pentacle connected five-phase IM supplied by a rectangular voltage
abstract: The presented article deals with a steady state analysis of a five-phase induction motor (IM) supplied by a five-legs voltage source inverter (VSI) with rectangular voltages. A complex Fourier-series is used to express the inverter output voltages, on the basis of which the relationship for the inverter output space phasor was derived. Assuming sinusoidal motor winding distribution, on the base of motor parameters the stator and rotor current space phasors are determined. At least the electromagnetic torque ripple waveforms for different operation IM states are investigated.

articleTitle: Dynamic objects detection of the respiratory epithelium based on image analysis
abstract: This paper deals with detection of the movement of the objects from the respiratory apparatus (cilia) based on image analysis. The theoretical part of article deals with an overview of the most widespread dynamic image segmentation methods and a proposal of final algorithm derived from optical flow. The work includes the portability of the individual methods and the possibility of using it to obtain information about the ciliary motility.

articleTitle: Utilization of finite state machine approach for smart region generation modelling
abstract: The paper describes the Finite State Machines (FSM) approach in a Smart Region's distributed energy sources modelling. It defines FSM models for a small hydro power plant, a cogeneration unit and a photovoltaic power plant. A comparison of simulation results obtained by FSM models and purely dynamic simulations models, from an execution time point of view, is presented as well.

articleTitle: Investigation of thermal performance of magnetic components in interleaved DC/DC converters
abstract: This paper deals with the investigation of the thermal behavior of magnetic components within boost converter. Instead of that, the trend of interleaving is considered as an alternative for the improvement of the electrical and mechanical properties of boost converters. For that purpose, 1-phase, 2-phase, 3-phase and 4-phase interleaved converters are being mutually compared. Design of individual topologies was done, while magnetic component (boost) inductor was modified from the magnetic core size point of view. It is seen that interleaving has a beneficial impact from a temperature point of view because the visible reduction of the magnetic component together with the reduction of component temperature is visible. The main outcome of this paper is a review of the procedure, which will enable to optimize magnetic components within interleaved topologies in future works.

articleTitle: Design of a control system for an intelligent building
abstract: This paper discusses about intelligent buildings and design of our own simple control system that will communicate with multiple actuators and sensors over Ethernet and to evaluate the measured values. The system consist of three devices based on Arduino Ethernet development boards and Quido ETH 4/4 board. This system can be used to control processes in intelligent buildings.

articleTitle: Fabrication technology of PDMS based cylindrical and structured microchannels for LOC
abstract: Cylindrically shaped microchannels are still challenging in lab-on-a-chip applications because of more laminar flow of biological samples and reagents inside. A simple, cheap and flexible technology to fabricate cylindrical and structured microchannels in polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) is presented here. We proposed an unconventional method, where photoresist of appropriate viscosity can be drawn into thin fibers of cylindrical shape at room temperature and formatted into various microfluidic channel templates. Also we present unique technology of patterning the prepared photoresist fiber by optical interference lithography. By embedding process of patterned photoresist fiber in liquid PDMS we obtained very interesting structured microchannels. The photoresist fibers and embossed PDMS microchannels exhibit excellent mechanical and surface characteristics suitable for microchannel structures and passive micromixers. Prepared microchannel structures are good candidates for using in different microfluidic and biomedical systems for simple integration on the PDMS based chips.

articleTitle: Real-time simulation of scaled propulsion unit for light electric vehicles
abstract: The paper describes the implementation of a realtime simulator of a light electric vehicle propulsion unit using scaled propulsion motor and scaled battery. In order to determine the optimum size of the motor and the battery pack this method is a valuable tool. This scaling flexibility can be used to build a relatively low cost test bench where a propulsion unit can be tested for different motors and batteries, using the same components but with different scaling gains. The Buckingham Pi Theorem is applied to calculate the appropriate scaling gains. Field Oriented Control (FOC) is used to control the Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (PMSM). The models of the control, PMSM and the battery are built using Matlab/Simulink and converted into a Dynamic-link library (DLL) file in order to be uploaded into the real-time processor of the Embedded Controller NI PXIe-8135. Different simulation scenarios are applied using NI VeriStand.

articleTitle: RealTime emulation of a three-phase vienna rectifier with unity power factor operations
abstract: In this paper a FPGA-based dynamic model of a three-phase Vienna Rectifier with unity power factor operations has been developed addressing applications as stationary chargers for electric vehicle or telecom rectifiers. Such a model has been implemented to be used in a Hardware In the Loop (HIL) system where the power converter has been replaced with an embedded system based on a FPGA board. The proposed system has been designed to test converter control algorithms in a fast and safe way. The proposed solution exploits an environment software platform with a high level abstraction, obtaining a good trade-off between accuracy and hardware resources, also allowing a faster prototyping procedure. The HIL implementation has been compared with that of the experimental rig, confirming a good agreement in terms of accuracy and dynamic behavior.

articleTitle: Comparison of converters using LLC and LCCT resonant tanks
abstract: In this paper, the circuit topologies of LLC resonant DC-DC converter and half-bridge LCCT resonant DC-DC converter are comparatively studied for different kind of applications. A comparison of efficiency, cost and behavior of these power converters is provided. Simulation models of LLC and LCCT circuits are created using magnetic and thermal models of individual components using PLECS simulation software. Based on the circuit investigation within critical operational conditions, short-circuit and overload states are analyzed.

articleTitle: Implementation of measured stroke volume within electromechanical analogy-based human body arterial model
abstract: Human arterial system simulation models represents a helpful tool for investigating blood pressure and blood flow propagating from the aorta towards upper and lower peripheral vessels. Real-life hemodynamic parameters are used as input for the arterial model based on electromechanical analogy. The mentioned parameters are determined from impedance cardiography measurements carried out on five human subjects. The theoretical model is thus individually adapted using real-life hemodynamic parameter values and the impact of stroke volume and heart rate changes on blood pressure and blood flow waveforms are investigated. We can conclude that the stroke volume influences especially the amplitude of the said curves, whereas the heart rate modifies shape thereof.

Author Keywords: model of the human arterial system

articleTitle: Conventional SiO2 and chalcogenide AS2S3 fiber Bragg grating sensors an comparison
abstract: In this paper we have numerically analyzed the application of chalcogenide fiber Bragg gratings as promising tools for sensing applications. Hence the chalcogenide materials are promising for using also in near IR regime over the 2 μm, the chalcogenide As2S3 grating parameters is compared with conventional SiO2 grating. Each parameter is calculated at typical communication wavelength 1550 nm. This paper is focused mainly on temperature, strain and pressure effects which caused change on Bragg wavelength and therefore change on the reflectance spectrum of these gratings.

articleTitle: 3D GMR sensor detection ability in nondestructive evaluation of austenitic biomaterials
abstract: This paper deals with nondestructive evaluation of concrete conductive biomaterials that are nowadays widely used on the field of biomedicine. The study focuses on detection ability of a commercial magnetic field sensor for detection of residual magnetic field of inspected biomaterials. The gained results are presented and discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Possible danger of massive charging of electric vehicles without its system management
abstract: This paper tries to show what consequences to grid will have when hundreds of thousands internal combustion engines cars will be replaced by electro mobiles. It describes possible charging patterns and how it would deal with immediate power capacity and total consumptions.

articleTitle: On-line monitoring of functional patient status in chronomagnetotherapy complex “Multimag”
abstract: The article considers methods and facilities of online and distance control of functional patient status in the process of magnetotherapy session. The ways to register bioelectrical signals in “Multimag” complex, to form pulse- and rhythmograms to determine the characteristics of heart rate variability and diagnostic indicators are shown. Different options to implement biotechnical feedback for magnetic action adaptation and treatment efficiency increase are offered.

articleTitle: Design of cybernetic model for glucose clamp techniques
abstract: Glucose clamp techniques are used in clinical studies to determine glucose metabolism indices. In order to “clamp”the blood glucose levels, the negative feedback principle is used to maintain glycemia at desired levels, depending on the specific clamp technique. The purpose of this study is to develop dynamical multivariable system model of glucose metabolism for analysis of input/output interactions using cybernetic principles. The structure of model is chosen to study the direct impact of insulin and glucose infusion rate on glucose and insulin levels in blood. The model is derived from the linearization of widely used Bergman minimal model. Multiple input-output interaction can then be further analyzed in order to determine the quality and robustness of existing control strategies or to develop new ones Simulations of a more complex physiological Sorensen model are used to validate the resulting model.

articleTitle: Cardiostimulator excitation signal generators in MATLAB and Simulink environment
abstract: Cardiostimulator treatment plays an important part in cardiovascular disease treatment. This is especially true in cases where medical treatment is not sufficient and the patient needs a heart transplant, however during the waiting period the heart must be supported by the said cardiostimulator. This article details our two developed MATLAB applications which can generate a suitable excitation signal for the testing of basic characteristics of implantable devices and the establishment of measurement labs for the mentioned purpose too.

articleTitle: Superposition of current and voltage harmonics
abstract: This paper deals with power quality that is aimed on voltage and current harmonics. The analysis describes the household appliances producing the harmonic interference, because they consist of semiconductor components. The next reason is that a large number of household appliances are operated in the same time. This harmonic interference has negative influence on grid. A simulation in program Matlab - Simulink was created based on the real measured data of these household appliances. The simulation serves to verify the principle of superposition of voltages and currents harmonics and their influence on the resulting shape of these parameters.

articleTitle: General concepts of teleoperated systems
abstract: This paper provides basic survey of teleoperated robotic systems and their characteristics. The aim of the paper is not to describe such robotic systems in details, but to provide basic information, which must be regarded during the design of such robot. Paper is focused on general description of functionality and characteristics of teleoperated robots. Especially safe issues are highlighted, because such robots suffers from the involvement of humans in the control scheme.

articleTitle: Dynamic current mode power supply with a 3P 4Q PFC module and with energy recuperation ability to the mains for feeding superconducting paricle accelerator magnets
abstract: This paper presents a developed four quadrant, three phase, AC to DC converter for dynamic mode, current source power supplies with ability of energy recuperation from the load to the mains. The developed converter will be a part of universal and modular platform for current source power supplies, feeding superconducting magnets in particle accelerators. The main advantages of the developed 4Q module are the unity power factor at the input and the energy recuperation ability from the superconducting magnets to the mains. This paper presents some design aspects, performances and test results of the developed 4Q PFC converter and the developed, new power supply concept.

articleTitle: Project based learning and simulation of setting a company to enhance business mindset of master engineer students and international cooperation skills
abstract: The contribution deals with some models for teaching entrepreneurship mainly at Engineering Universities and Colleges particularly describing the case at Faculty of Materials Science and Technology in Slovakia. The “Entrepreneurship Studies” is provided as an obligatory elective course for students of various Study Programs in the first year at their Master degree. Two-year period of piloting the new model of teaching the course to enhance students' business mindset revealed pros and cons of the approach that has been applied. Finally, situation in Entrepreneurship Education at a Russian University (Izhevsk state technical university of the name M.T. Kalashnikov) are described and some future proposal for international cooperation skills development are presented.

articleTitle: Interleaved boost converter with modified inductor
abstract: This paper describes dual interleaved boost converter with magnetically coupled inductors, while additional inductor is used for magnetic flux reset of the core during converter operation. Main focus within presented research was given on the investigation of steady-state operation of proposed converter in terms of voltage gain characteristic investigation, power loss analysis and experimental verification of received simulation results. It was discovered that proposed converter can be designed for target application where high voltage gain is required together with strict requirements on voltage stability (output voltage ripple and voltage stability). The adjustment of voltage gain can be done in two possible ways, e.g. through duty - cycle variation or by the turns-ratio modification between individual inductors. The 1 kW prototype was designed to test theoretical analysis. The results demonstrates that proposed converter achieves very high voltage gain (1:8), while for designed prototype the peak efficiency reaches >96% even two additional diodes and one winding were implemented within converter's main circuit.

articleTitle: Study of structural arrangement in ferrofluid by dielectric and acoustic spectroscopy
abstract: In the paper two methods of investigation of ferrofluid in magnetic and electric fields were used, namely the acoustic and the dielectric spectroscopy. The measurements were done at temperature 15 °C. The effect of structural changes in ferrofluid upon the effect of a magnetic field by the acoustic spectroscopy was studied. At jump change of the magnetic field to 100, 200 and 300 mT a continuous change of the acoustic attenuation caused by an aggregation of magnetic nanoparticles to new structures was observed. The changes in dielectric parameters and structural arrangement of magnetic nanoparticles in ferrofluid upon the effect of magnetic and electric fields have been studied by the dielectric spectroscopy, too. The frequency dependence of dissipation factor was measured by a capacitance method within the frequency range from 1 mHz to 10 kHz at the application of a magnetic and an electric fields. The magneto-dielectric effect was also observed.

articleTitle: Use of tensor construction of Markov chains when evaluating observed feature of E-SRS
abstract: During the creation of electronic safety related systems great attention should be paid not only to functional requirements for system but also to safety and dependability requirements. Proving required safety and dependability features of E-SRS requires not only a choice of a suitable method but also the creation of a model, describing an observed feature of E-SRS, according to factors influencing the observed feature. At complex multilevel systems it is usually complicated to directly create the model that would describe the observed feature of E-SRS, resp. a probability of a mistake appearing during the creation of the complicated model is great. The paper deals with an evaluation of the observed feature of multilevel E-SRS by Markov chains. The creation of the final model is based on the application of the tensor product and the tensor sum to simple Markov models that describe the observed feature of individual subsystems of which the E-SRS is composed. The paper also deals with an issue of the state explosion problem which comes from a tensor construction of Markov chains.

articleTitle: Analysis of channel propagation models based on calculated and measured data
abstract: In this research various propagation models are analyzed and compared according to both of calculated and measured results. These propagation models depend on location, frequency range and clutter type such as urban, suburban and countryside. The propagation models have been proposed at the operating frequency of 900 MHz. The interaction between the electromagnetic waves and the environment reduces the signal strength, which is sent from transmitter to receiver that causes the path loss. It was noticed from the obtained results that SUI model showed the lowest path loss values in urban environment.

articleTitle: The comparison of selected fire scenarios with TuSim
abstract: The paper deals with an effect of the technological equipment on safety of humans and property in the tunnel. The main objective is risk analysis based on scenario's analysis of an accident event. Simulations of designed models are performed with the hardware/software (HW/SW) tool called TuSim. The paper focuses on the worst cases and describes a simulation experiment through TuSim and the comparison with another approaches.

articleTitle: Design and preparation of polymer components for microspectrometer on the chip
abstract: In this paper, we present design and preparation of polymer components for microspectrometer fabrication on a chip. The graphical program was used to design novel components in 3D arrangement. In experimental we used two-photon polymerization for direct writing of designed structures in IP-Dip photoresist material. Shape and morphological properties of prepared devices were investigated by scanning electron microscope (SEM). Finally, optical properties were examined by diffraction measurement with red laser.

articleTitle: Utilization of FBG's in experimental weighing in motion systems
abstract: In the context of the development of technology and systems of internet of things the requirements for collecting, processing and transmitting signals are increasing in all areas of society. The photonics solutions play and will play an important role. This is significant; both on the signal transmission side-mainly in the backbone networks as well as on the data collection side, especially for machine-to-machine communication. This paper is focuses on the use of optical sensors and their application in transport systems. It shows the possibilities of introducing them into such complex systems as weighing in motion. This paper deals with usability of optical sensors and can be used in the design of advanced photonic sensor systems and networks applicable to internet of things solutions or intelligent transport system based on fiber optics. Presented technology of optical sensors based on fibre Bragg gratings has been applied as experimental weighing in motion system. For the needs of this experimental system, a unique embedded sensor layout structure has been proposed. This experimental system is capable to obtain maximally 2000 data per second.

articleTitle: Robust sliding mode observer application in vector control of induction motor
abstract: During last years, sensorless control is one of the most favorite field in control of AC machines, especially induction motor drives. Sensorless control means that an encoder is replaced by estimated speed from an observer or an estimator. Sensorless control reduces cost and increases the reliability of the system. However, the accuracy of the observer or estimator depends on induction motor parameters. In this paper, the robust sliding mode observer with estimated rotor and stator resistances is investigated. The proof of stability of the algorithm is also presented. The robust sliding mode observer is verified through simulations and experiments with an induction motor drive. Some of control methods such as PI control and sliding mode control are used in the experiments.

articleTitle: Boresight calibration of a multi-sensor system for UAS photogrammetry
abstract: The calibration of multi-sensor systems to facilitate direct georeferencing is essential for ensuring high accuracy photogrammetry products. Integrated solutions require estimations and compensations of misalignments - positional and/or angular - between individual sensors. This paper discusses the calibration of angular misalignments, or boresight angles, caused by the inaccurate alignment of the image and body frame. Such a task is performed via field calibration, enabling us to estimate boresight angles using data from a real UAS mission. A UAS equipped with a custom-built multi-sensor system, comprising a state-of-the-art technology in navigation systems, was employed to collect aerial data across the test area. In order to obtain reference data for the calibration, thirty ground control points were distributed in the area, and the exterior orientation of every image was estimated through aerial triangulation. In addition to the boresight calibration, the attitude measurement accuracy was assessed and discussed.

articleTitle: Optimal design of MHD pump
abstract: Optimization of an induction pump is carried out. Based on numerical simulation, weight-and-size parameters are reduced and thrust of pump is increased. The problem of optimization is realized using the open-source package of numerical modeling Agros Suite. The task is formulated in an electromagnetic approximation, neglecting a non-uniform distribution of a velocity in a pipe. The saturation of the magnetic circuit and back iron is taken into account in a quasi-static formulation. The problem is solved in two-dimensional formulation, taking into account the transverse edge effect by coefficient of Bolton. The effectiveness of optimization algorithms implemented in Agros Suite (BOBYQA, BayestOpt, Limbo, NSGA-2) and Comsol Multiphysics (Nelder-Mead, BOBYQA, Coordinate Search) is compared.

articleTitle: Issues of integration of the inversion formula while calculating the distribution of output values of the GERT network
abstract: A law of division of a continuous output value of a GERT network having polynomial computational complexity is found via the inversion formula integration method. The scaling of the probability distributions of random values acting as the weights of the arcs of the GERT network by compressing their characteristic functions is applied. The distribution of the output value of the GERT network is transformed to a discrete form using an intermediate transformation.

articleTitle: Supplying electricity to service and business complexes
abstract: Many analyses of factors are conducted while planning investments that will allow maximal use of potential of a complex in the future. These actions also include the issues of availability of energy, particularly electric energy, its quality and costs of building electric power infrastructure. Supply systems, values of demand power and diversity of requirements of reliability of power, as well as options of using specific solutions are considered while making selections. Economic issues related to accepted solution and their impact on future use of a designed complex are not considered enough. The authors of this publication raise issues related to quality of electric energy in supply systems of service and business complexes that may considerably lower profitability of administering Business Park complexes. The authors used Poleczki Business Park Warszawa as an example of interferences in such complexes.

articleTitle: Comparative mode control of a system with two-position controller
abstract: This paper deals with mathematical analysis of two position control of a continuous system. Design of a control circuit is based on full operating cycle for a system of a second order. As an improvement of this control, set-point is implemented to the control circuit. The input switching mode is then based on comparison of the output state of a system and the set-point value. The paper presents complete mathematical analysis of this comparative mode of a system with two-position controller.

articleTitle: Calculation of radiation field iso-surfaces using numerical continuation method
abstract: The paper deals with calculation of iso-lines of radiation-field from isotropic rectangular source using pseudo arc-length continuation. The proposed approach is demonstrated on fire-safety application.

articleTitle: Conditioning of light microscope for advanced methods of ciliary dyskinesia diagnostics
abstract: This article discusses about the RGBA (red-green-blue-amber) LEDs brightness control. RGBA LEDs consist of four different colors used to illuminate samples in a microscope. The first part of the article is a brief procedure for designing a hardware part of the illumination of the microscope. In the next part of the article, we describe specifically the used LEDs and drivers that control them. The entire hardware system is built on the Arduino Nano microcontroller. Besides the hardware part of the microscope, the software interface was also solved in the LabVIEW environment. The last part of the article discusses the front panel of the application's graphical interface and its components, as well as the practical application of a light-controlled optical microscope in a medical environment. Optical microscope can be used to measure CBF (ciliary beat frequency) of the cilia of the respiratory apparatus using stroboscopic effect.

articleTitle: Usefulness mathematical modeling in the process of assessing the environmental impact of linear energetic constructions
abstract: Overground and underground power transmission and distribution lines of 110 kV to 400 kV as linear energy constructions are subject to assessment of their environmental impact. The impact of electromagnetic fields (EMF) must also be assessed in the assessment. The issue of the protection of the health of the population in the Slovak Republic (SR) in connection with exposure to the electromagnetic field is dealt with by Decree of the Ministry of Health no. 534/2007 Col. In accordance with that Decree, scientifically valid standards, procedures and recommendations are used to assess, measure or calculate exposure to the electromagnetic field to determine EMF values.
