Mathematical modelling is one of the possibilities of objectivizing the levels of electromagnetic fields in the vicinity of power lines, which provides a number of advantages and options for a detailed assessment of their impact from an EMF perspective.

articleTitle: Design of reconfigurable robot
abstract: Reconfigurable robot is solution for unknown environment with various obstacles. Also energy consumption is better, when suitable locomotion mode is selected. Proposed service robot is able to locomotes via using of wheels or legs. The design of such structure has several advantage as better ability to cross the various types of terrain. The prototype of the designed robot will be used as educational tool.

articleTitle: Waste lighting heat generation as the key process to design the only technical device needed in interiors
abstract: This paper searches the reliable technical solutions for the transfer of the generated waste heat from modern light sources. It presents the basic principles for a more effective technical solution as a key way to increase the needed technical system utilization and to improve the electric and thermal engineering connectivity in buildings. The designed device represents a higher level of energy efficiency with two ways of waste heat utilization. It uses a light-emitting diode (LED) as a source of light and heat. With multifunction property able to provide all necessary conditions for life in interior. Main positive and negative aspects of a novel technical system using this device are described.

articleTitle: Investigation of electrical properties of Ca(PO2)2 metaphosphate glass using electrical conductivity measurements
abstract: The sample of metaphosphate glass Ca(PO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> was investigated using the electrical conductivity measurements in the range of frequency 10 Hz -2 MHz and over range of temperatures 692 K-825 K. The aim of this work is investigation of modulus formalism which has been used for characterize the frequency dependent conductivity and dielectric relaxation process. Dielectric relaxation and modulus formalism are explored through real and imaginary impedance measurements.

articleTitle: Beauty in physics — potential for education
abstract: Physical laws have beauty characterized by symmetry, productivity and simplicity. We discuss importance of beauty in fundamental physics with an example of the theory of electromagnetic interactions. If this subject is properly presented to the students, it can help motivate their effort to understand things at a deeper level.

articleTitle: Laboratory complexes to study properties of materials and structures of solid state electronics
abstract: In this paper we present results of our developments in computer laboratory works for students studying materials of micro- and nanoelectronics. We developed several works to investigate dielectric permittivity and loss tangent, conductivity of metals and alloys, volume and surface resistance of dielectric materials, breakdown of dielectrics, properties of magnetic materials and thermal analysis of metal alloys. These works could be used for simulating physical processes in solid state materials. Virtual laboratory complexes developed in the environment of engineering graphical programming NI LabVIEW.

articleTitle: Measurement complex on the basis of AFM for investigating charge carrier distribution in semiconductor barrier structures
abstract: Measurement complex on the basis of atomic force microscope for investigating electrophysical properties of semiconductor barrier structures is developed and described in this paper. Electromechanical model of point barrier metal-semiconductor contact is clarified. A method to measure electrical capacitance of point barrier contact is described. We developed software to control measuring complex and obtained data about distribution of charge carriers in structures with quantum wells.

articleTitle: The importance of physics courses for students of faculty of electrical engineering
abstract: The paper informs about the importance of physics courses for students of Faculty of Electrical Engineering during the first academic year. Students at technical universities generally have significantly low prior knowledge in both mathematical and physical knowledge at the beginning of their study. Students' participation in physics courses is seen as one of the factors contributing not only to enhancing knowledge of physics but also to their better orientation in the study. The standardized FCI test was used in order to analyse students' concepts at the beginning and the end of physics courses (pre and post-test). We analyse the results of testing the physics knowledge of preparatory Course of Physics and compulsory courses The Introduction to Physics and Physics I.

articleTitle: Fuzzy model-based speed observer for sensorless induction motor drive with PWM-DTC
abstract: The paper deals with application of fuzzy logic in model-based rotor speed observer for sensorless induction motor drive. Stability analysis of selected observer is described in the first part. Fuzzy logic is applied to adjust parameters of proportional-integral adaption algorithm in rotor speed adaption mechanism. The third part is description of a laboratory stand with the induction motor drive and load unit that was used for an experimental verification of the speed observer with application of fuzzy logic. Expected properties of sensorless control of induction motor drive are confirmed by experimental results.

articleTitle: Analysis and planning of specialists resources to repair and maintenance of complex technical products at the basis of Petri networks
abstract: This paper is concerned with the usage of Petri networks as a kind of marked graph to evaluate production process efficiency. General model of production process is given. General characteristics are calculated.

articleTitle: Multi-level simulation model of the wireless power transfer system
abstract: This article deals with the design of a multi-level simulation model of the wireless power transfer (WPT) system. The model is designed to determine the optimal operating characteristics of the WPT system. The primary part of the model aimed at modeling of electromagnetic fields, specifically the reconfigurable system of coils, which seek to determine their self-inductance and mutual inductance. These parameters are further used in the electrical circuit model of the WPT system.

articleTitle: Applications of process control system with (SCADA) and PID controller
abstract: This paper present some results of supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) as well as ways how to maintain the flow of water in a tank using the Proportional, Integral and Derivative (PID) controller based on a digital signal processing device are presented in the paper. Focused on the proportional gain, or just gain, sensitive of the valve change to given errors, and controller action. The concept of this process is to control the flow of water in the tank and to make sure, the flow of water always follow the range that has been set. The collected data were analysed and compared to the actual and desired performance of the system. Evaluation of the system to adjusting the certain flow and set point value more accurately. The PID controller calculates an error value as difference between a measured process variable and a desired set point. The controller attempts to minimize the error by adjusting the process control inputs. In addition, to achieve complex mathematical functions to compare a set of data to the set point and subtraction functions. The water flow measurement and control are essential for effective operation of water treatment and supply units.

articleTitle: Autotransformer design with zig-zag connection Zna0
abstract: The autotransformer which is supplied by network without neutral wire must be loaded symmetrically. Already small unsymmetrical load causes significant voltage imbalance and overvoltage. When the fully loading of one phase is required, the zigzag autotransformer connection must be used. This paper describes the behavior and design of autotransformers under unsymmetrical loading conditions.

articleTitle: Subsurface cracks evaluation using pulsed eddy current and cross correlation
abstract: Detection capability of pulsed eddy current testing device is described and illustrated with a set of of an artificial deap surface and subsurface defects in an electrically conductive steel plate. The investigated eddy current probe is of a differential type, consisting of one excitation and two sensing coils with a ferrite magnetic circuit. The numerical solution is carried out in the COMSOL Multiphysics using Magnetic field and Electrical circuit modules. The results are verified by performing laboratory experiment. Postprocessing of output signal is done by cross-correlation with set of reference pulses. Effect of the depth of subsurface defect on output differential signal is then analyzed and discussed.

articleTitle: Effect of optimized wireless energy transfer system on human cells
abstract: Wireless power transfer and issues relevant to wireless charging of various types of electronic devices are still important and emerging trends in electrical engineering (1). Regarding wireless power transfer, each application requires several self-specific operational properties or transfer characteristics. A possible way to influence these parameters lies in the configuration of the main circuit of compensation network of wireless energy transfer (WET) system (2). A very important parameters of the WET system is (i) the efficiency of the entire charging system as well as (ii) the effect of optimized WET systems on living organisms.

articleTitle: Surrogate modelling technique in multi-parametric laser welding process
abstract: A possibility of using surrogate model for fast determining weld depth in multi-parametric hybrid laser welding process (laser welding with induction preheating) is studied. The dependence of weld depth on laser beam power and velocity of its movement is investigated. For selected combinations of laser power and speed, FEM simulations of 3D coupled problem combining heat transfer and electromagnetic field are performed. The surrogate model is then created based on results allowing to predict depth for any combination of power and speed. Main motivation to use surrogate modeling technique is to substantially save the computational time.

articleTitle: Control strategy of cooler for diminishing dimensions and extending service lifetime of inverter
abstract: The paper deals with the construction design and thermal simulation analysis of double three-phase converter suitable for electric vehicles. It gives a discussion on basic mechanical design and electric topology having both strong influence on electro-thermal operability. Finally, the paper presents thermal analyses of the converter operated at specified loading profile and discusses its impact on the converter lifetime.

articleTitle: Modeling metrological testing methods for analog-digital conversions
abstract: The article considers automated computer modeling metrological testing methods of analog-digital conversions based on the formation of input action in the form high-precision reference signal, its movement in specified area, the registration of output coded samples array and further statistical analysis of measurements results.

articleTitle: Determination of nanocapillaries dimensions in insulative oil impregnated electrotechnical pressboard
abstract: The paper presents a stand for measuring the oil absorption rate during impregnation of electrotechnical pressboard or other porous materials. The stand allows for accurate record of absorbed oil volume and the time in which it was absorbed. It was found that the time needed to complete impregnating of pressboard is about 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> s. At this time, pressboard absorbs the insulating oil in a volume of approx. 25.6% its volume. This means that the free spaces occupy about 25.6% of pressboard volume. The testing of the pressboard free surface showed that it is about 10 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> per cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Based on these data, it was found that the average value of capillary diameter in the pressboard is about 25.6 nm.

articleTitle: Simulation of 6/4 and 12/8 switched reluctance motor using direct torque control
abstract: The paper presents the simulation of switched reluctance motors with a number of poles 2p<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>/2p<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> = 12/8 and 6/4 using the ANSYS software. The simulated machines have same dimensions and they work with the identical saturation of the magnetic circuit. Models of the motor based on finite element analysis are designed by ANSYS Maxwell. Motors are controlled by the direct torque control. Using FEM models of motors allows the ANSYS Simplorer. Simulation results, as the cooperation ANSYS software packages are included in this document as well. Simulation results of both models as the cooperation ANSYS software are presented as well.

articleTitle: A novel zero voltage transition non-isolated bidirectional converter for energy storage applications
abstract: This paper presents a new approach to realize zero voltage transition in a non-isolated bidirectional DC/DC converter for the applications of battery back-up systems in electric vehicles. The proposed converter works in either boost or buck mode. The main characteristics of all switching devices are turned at zero voltage transition, which is achieved with the inclusion of resonant auxiliary devices with the conventional bidirectional converter. This converter has low switching losses, low voltage stress and better efficiency. This paper presented operation principles simulation results and its experimental validations by a 100V/1.5kW laboratory prototype.

articleTitle: Design and control of a CNC device designed for the application of viscous materials
abstract: This article deals with the design and practical realization of a CNC device designed for the application of viscous materials, such as a thermal conducting paste. According to the given specification, the choice of a suitable mechanical construction and the design of a mechanism for extruding the paste from the tube are solved. A separate part is the choice of a suitable drive and design of electronic circuits to control it. The last part contains the selection of the appropriate control program and its modification.

articleTitle: Design proposal for heating element of biological microscope
abstract: This paper deals with the development design proposal of a heating system for maintaining a required temperature of a microscopic biological sample. The need for maintaining a specific temperature of a biological sample is given by the viability of the microorganism depending on their temperature. Meeting the conditions for changing or maintaining the required temperature is especially necessary in cases such as monitoring the growth of microorganisms and temperature dependent mutations. In this paper, the best possible design of the heating element is investigated through thermal simulation analysis. Consequently, the proposal for an appropriate control algorithm for the selected heating system arrangement is given together with its verification.

articleTitle: Investigation of birefringence of elastically deformed poly(methyl methacrylate)
abstract: In the paper we present the results of an experimental investigation of birefringence of a poly(methyl methacrylate) small blocks that are subject to applied mechanical stress. First, the investigated sample is placed between two crossed linear polarizers that effectively polarize visible light within the range from 470 nm to 750 nm, and birefringence of the unloaded sample is measured. After that a load causing elastic deformation is gradually applied to the sample. A white-light source is used for investigation and response of the polarizer-stressed sample-analyzer optical system is detected via optical fiber connected to an optical spectral analyzer. The measured intensity of light transmitted through the optical system is plotted as function of wavelength for various loads. Analysis of the obtained spectra led to the dependences of the normalized intensity of light on the load as well as the birefringence on the load for various wavelengths. The character of the dependences indicates the possibility of utilization the material as a basis for an element of a sensor of pressure, stress, small deformations or for weight measuring.

articleTitle: Decreasing the power consumption of buildings with utilization of lighting control
abstract: Today there are increasing efforts to decrease the power consumption of buildings. Even simple and inexpensive solutions can significantly influence the energy consumption. This paper describes the issue of power consumption of buildings. The main area of interest is focused on the lighting. The data, that are used to draft the concept of power consumption reduction, were obtained by measurement and simulations. Measures based on these data were taken in order to reduce the power consumption needed to achieve the required illuminence level and they were verified with measurements and simulations.

articleTitle: Improved design of switched capacitors for power electronics converters
abstract: This paper brings the improved design of switched capacitors for power electronics converters. The desired value of capacity is obtained by switching between two capacitors with a specific duty cycle. The old method for calculating the value of the switched capacity and the duty cycle is based on energy conservation. This method, however, as shown below, does not provide a precise result. For this reason, a new averaging method is derived. The practical use of the switched capacitors is shown on a two-phase load, with auxiliary phase current advancing.

articleTitle: Measuring system for analysis of transformer moisture
abstract: This article is focused about for electronic proposal measuring system of moisture analysis by return voltage method (RVM) for power oil transformers. RVM method is wide state specifying method which is not set in standards but in many cases is a method which is determining a clear and exact result. The results have mainly shows moisture content, content of conductive impurities in oil and degree of aging of paper insulation impact.

articleTitle: Experimental method to measure built-in electric fields in multilayer barrier homo- and heterostructures
abstract: In this paper we linked electrophysical properties of multilayer barrier structures based on crystalline and disordered semiconductors with density of electronic states localized in a mobility gap and their energy distribution. We propose experimental method to investigate built-on electric field distribution and its mathematical model. A measuring equipment to realize this method and used test structures is described. The obtained results are analyzed. We marked directions for further researches to improve the method.

articleTitle: Distance educational technologies in a discipline “Electroengineering and electronics”
abstract: The experience to use distance learning course “Electroengineering and electronics” while organizing academic process for the students of different training directions and different forms of study is presented. Distance educational technologies providing complete and visual presentation of training materials, their fast adaptation according to certain tasks and giving broad possibilities for a teacher to control and assess the results of students discipline mastering are shown.

articleTitle: Modeling and development of grid node with slotted hole configuration and extended charge parameters for specialized gas discharged current breaker
abstract: The article presents the results of the research in the field of modeling and development of gas discharged current breaker grid node with extended charge parameters for the generator of high-voltage pulses with inductive energy storage. The modeling has shown that the change of grid node holes geometry doesn't lead to the deterioration of electrical strength index. The advantages of gas discharged current breaker with the developed grid node operating in high-voltage pulse generator are described. 3D model of grid node produced is given. The comparison of grid node developed with the existing structures is given.

articleTitle: Electrical and acoustic properties of solid-state glass electrolytes
abstract: Solid-state electrolytes have become of a notable interest in a number of applications of electrical systems for energy storage and harvesting, and all solid-state rechargeable batteries, in particular. They possess key advantages with respect to liquid electrolytes such that they are non-contaminant and do not have flammable organic compounds, thus reducing toxicity and the risk of explosions, and they may also work as an effective separator between the electrode materials. An ideal electrolyte must have a pure ionic conductivity and high chemical and thermal stability under the conditions of operation and, within the inorganic solid electrolyte materials, glasses may offer additional improvements due to their inherent nature, without grain boundaries and great variability in both chemical composition and shape. There are well-known efficient ways to improve the performance of glasses as solid electrolytes through their chemical composition, e.g. by increasing the amount of charge carriers, introducing highly polarizable anions or through the use of secondary glass former elements. However, the study of the mechanisms of conduction for each system becomes a critical issue when optimizing the properties of the researched materials. We will present here a review on the application of electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and acoustic attentuation spectroscopy for the study of a series of glass systems showing ionic conductivity, and which combination may allow one to establish appropriate links between the atomic glass structure and the different mobile species that contribute to the conduction mechanism. We will summarize the results obtained in phosphate glasses, oxynitride glasses (LiPON) and mixed-former glasses (Li<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O-Na<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O-B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>), where in all cases we found strong correlations between the acoustic relaxation phenomena and the energetics of ionic conduction as well as with the strength of the glass network. Meanwhile impedance data in bulk amorphous systems only provide an activation energy value related to the average mobility of the conducting species, the use of acoustic attenuation does also allow for the distinction of several relaxation processes that may well be associated different ionic species or structural environments of the glass network.

articleTitle: Interdisciplinary cooperation — Pillar of engineering study attractiveness
abstract: The attractiveness of engineering study has been long an issue for consideration as the secondary school students usually argue about the demandingness of study at technical universities. The contribution puts forward several possibilities of enhancing the popularization of such a study via close interdisciplinary cooperation and involving thus the students in project work performed at the Student Research Conference or real projects.

articleTitle: Influence of housing developments on voltage quality in distribution point
abstract: This paper describes the issues of housing developments' influence on voltage quality in distribution point. Main focus is on the connection possibilities of planned housing developments with specific suggestions. Further, the voltage quality of measured objects and daily load of existing housing developments are evaluated by the detailed analysis. Measured values were used to create simulation model. The simulation model was created in Matlab - Simulink. The created model is used to find out all consequences of the current harmonics on voltage quality in distribution point.

articleTitle: The effect of external pressure on partial discharges and post-breakdown stages in LUKOSIOL
abstract: The characteristics of internal partial discharges in LUKOSIOL as a function of the applied voltage and the external pressure have been measured. The partial discharge measurements were performed with the help of Phase Resolved Partial Discharge Analyzer. The negative charge of partial discharge increased with the voltage and radically decreases at higher pressures. The pressure also caused an increase of the breakdown voltage and had influence on the development of post-breakdown stages — a vapor channel. From this strong dependence on the external pressure of the discharge characteristic results that pre-breakdown stage are connected with the gas phase. The time development of vapor channel was recorded by a high-speed camera.

articleTitle: A new era in simulation
abstract: The finite element method in conjunction with advanced material models, circuit simulators and control systems enhanced with power of current computers and numerical methods brings new possibilities for digital prototypes. Combining on-line operational data from working products with digital information about those products enables the digital twin and promises to take simulation into a new era. The paper introduces the ANSYS software tools designed for complex digital real-time prototypes.

articleTitle: MATLAB total academic headcount — features & experience
abstract: At almost every university around the world, MATLAB system is used extensively in teaching, research, and student projects in all fields of engineering, science, economics, and finance. More than 1 000 of these universities has already upgraded to a Total Academic Headcount (TAH) license. This type of license provides a full suite of MATLAB products to all students and university staff for use in the classroom or lab, as well as for use in off-line work in the field research or at home. There are 3 universities with the TAH license in Slovakia and the Czech Republic till now. Our goal is to provide information about TAH features and our experience arising from 1 year of TAH usage.

articleTitle: CAN BUS demonstration panel and its visualization using modular instrumentation
abstract: Signals in modern cars from sensors, control units, and signals for actuators are transmitted through buses. Controller Area Network (CAN) is the most common of these automotive data buses which is also used in industry because of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC). For a demonstration of this communication for education purpose, the instrument panel and its visualization were created. Demonstration panel contains gateway which simulates signals from the electronic control unit (ECU), accelerator pedal and Skoda instrument cluster. This instrument cluster shows engine speed, vehicle speed, coolant temperature and position of servo drive in two turbochargers. For data acquisition from CAN BUS a modular system CompactRio with a module for CAN BUS from National Instruments is used. The whole application is created in visual programming language LabVIEW using FPGA module. For visualization, CAN BUS communication is filtered and processed, to obtain three message objects to observe required data for visualization instrument cluster and accelerator pedal position.

articleTitle: Basic measurements of DC properties of nanocomposites (FeCoZr)x(SiOy)(100−x)
abstract: The paper presents the results of preliminary measurements of DC conductivity of metal - dielectric grain nanocomposites with chemical composition (FeCoZr)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>(SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(100-x)</sub>. Samples of materials with metallic phase contents x<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>=58.2 at.%, X<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>=67.0 at.% and X<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>=76.3 at.% prepared by the ion-beam sputtering of targets consisting of a Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">45</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">45</sub>Zr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">45</sub> alloy plate and SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> dielectric strips. The process was carried out in an argon atmosphere. The DC measurements were carried out in the temperature range from 20 K to 375 K. On this basis, the activation energies of electrons in individual cases were determined. It was found that there are three temperature ranges in which there is a change in the activation energy, which indicates a minimum of three types of potential wells between which electron tunneling occurs.

articleTitle: Offline programming of robot model with virtual environment support
abstract: Offline programming with the use of a virtual robot technology operates as if you had a real robot on your computer. Offline programming is the best way how to maximalize the return of investments of robotic workplaces. Programming of a robot on PC without the need of production stop is enabled by software for simulation and offline. It also enables to prepare robot programmes in advance, what increases overall productivity.

articleTitle: Smart monitoring of the emergencies by cyber-physical systems
abstract: The paper suggests a technology of smart-monitoring of the emergencies by cyber-physical systems for monitoring natural and anthropogenic emergencies, providing information and algorithmic support for a cyber-physical system of forest-fire monitoring. We also provide hierarchical structures of components for a cyber-physical system of forest-fire monitoring, so as to reduce the risk of decision making. The methodology is implemented as development of intellectual telecommunications structures on the base of the MB 7707 neuroprocessor systems that can undergo training in conditions of uncertainty.

articleTitle: Identification of static objects in the respiratory epithelium
abstract: The article deals with methods of detection of microscopic objects in video sequences while using the techniques of image processing and segmentation. It is focused on searching for static objects of interest - cilia of respiratory epithelium, with emphasis on elimination of the false-positive detections, i.e. detections of image artefacts. The article describes currently used segmentation techniques in the field of digital image processing, while besides the description of basic principles it also illustrates the application of particular methods into investigated images. The proposed algorithm for identifying objects of interest is described too. Finally, obtained results are analysed mainly from the accuracy point of view, summed up and compared to other so far used techniques.

articleTitle: Numerical models of array of electroacoustic transducers in anechoic chamber
abstract: Numerical modeling of acoustic field produced by a set of common commercial loudspeakers is carried out. The goal is to obtain a time-dependent level of acoustic pressure in the microphone. The continuous mathematical model is derived from the physical laws and is considered for the ideal fluids with properties of a perfect continuum. Results of the model derived from pressure acoustics and data obtained from measurement are compared.

articleTitle: A study of the rotor design influence in power factor value of ORSynRM
abstract: This paper presents the optimal design of a novel synchronous reluctance motor with outer rotor for determination the effect of rotor pole shape in the machine's performances. The investigation has been made in order to find the possible aspects to improve the power factor with refining rotor dimensions without added permanent magnet. Starting from the classical design of rotor pole implemented in Flux 2D, a finite element analysis software and the optimal design procedure implemented in Matlab, a complex co-simulation was accomplishing to obtain an outer rotor structures that increase the machine's performance: saliency ratio, power factor and torque density. The obtained results have never been presented in the past literature and its represents a useful starting point for the following analysis of outer rotor synchronous reluctance machines.

articleTitle: Calculation of the discrete random output value distribution in GERT networks
abstract: A method with polynomial computational complexity for finding the law for the distribution of a discrete output value of a GERT network is proposed. Simplifying transformations of the GERT network structure with a step-by-step exclusion of nodes and an equivalent calculation of the characteristic functions that describe the arcs of the GERT network are used.

articleTitle: Optimizing the localization of gamma radiation point sources using a UGV
abstract: The paper is concerned with the autonomous robotic measurement of gamma radiation and the localization of its sources. The objective is to find techniques that allow faster localization compared to mapping along parallel lines. To achieve this, an unmanned ground vehicle (UGV) is utilized; the device is equipped with a sensitive dual-probe radiation detection system and a module for precise self-localization and navigation. The suggested solution involves exploring the region of interest along circular trajectories and estimating the sources' parameters, the coordinates in particular. The estimation accuracy is then increased using the Gauss-Newton method. The approach was verified through experiments in real conditions; the achieved result consists in a threefold decrease of the time requirement while the localization accuracy remains comparable to that acquired by the radiation mapping. The benefits of the presented research comprise the qualitative expansion of the radiation protection domain and also the applicability of several utilized algorithms in other fields or activities, including, for example, the autonomous robotic inspection of industrial facilities.

articleTitle: A visual attention operator for playing Pac-Man
abstract: The paper explores the use of reinforcement learning in tasks that involve image-like (but not necessarily raw-pixel) state representations. It proposes a visual attention operator, related to the concept of visual attention presented in previous works. The operator is tested on the game of Pac-Man, where it allows the use of the same agent with various game layouts, no matter what their dimensions (and thus the size of the image-like representation) are. It is shown that the approach is able to summarize information present in the original representation into a fixed-size glimpse and that the approach is able to outperform several more direct approaches.

articleTitle: Idea of learning context system using iBeacons
abstract: Today, electronics is present in all sectors including educational institutions. Modern technology can greatly make life easier for students and educators. The following text deals with a system built on indoor localization, its capabilities and links to existing e-learning systems. The aim of the paper is to verify this system in practice and to analyze the acquired data.

articleTitle: Design of power quality analyzer
abstract: This paper deals with hardware and software design of Power quality analyzer, which is capable of measuring in both three-phase and one-phase power lines. The designed device can be used for the educational purposes in the field of electrical energy quality. It contains also description individual parts of proposed power quality analyzer (i.e. hardware and software) for measuring electrical parameters. The proposed Power quality analyzer can be also used for estimation of power quality in electrical network.

articleTitle: The impact of light sources operation on accuracy of the intelligent metering system
abstract: This article describes impact of light sources to accuracy the intelligent metering system. The light sources contains the electronics converters and ballasts. These devices generate harmonics to distribution grid and they have impact to accuracy of the measurement. It is describes the verification of the measurement with using a programmable source witch can generate harmonics. There are two approaches how to measure the error: the first one is according to an amplitude law. The second approaches is measurement with using real harmonics witch were measured witch network power analyser.

articleTitle: The radio signal phase estimate efficiency under the fast fades
abstract: Our study is concerned with the narrow-band radio signals phase estimation when these signals are deformed by fades and observed against white noise. Unlike the approach presented in the popular studies, we presume these fades to be fast, i.e. the fades correlation time is much less than the signal duration. We also consider the amplitude and the phase of the fading signal component as having Rayleigh and uniform probability distributions, correspondingly, that fits the case of the Rice fades. We find the analytical expressions for the probability density, as well as for the bias (systematic error) and the variance (error mean square) of the phase estimation in the presence of fades. We also analyze the influence of the fades depth on the efficiency of the radio signal phase measurement.

articleTitle: On registration of vector maps with known correspondences
abstract: Data association and registration is an important and actively researched topic in robotics. This paper deals with registration of two sets of line segments, which is especially useful in mapping applications. Our method is non-iterative, finding an optimal transformation in a single step, in a time proportional only to a number of the corresponding line segments. The procedure also provides diagnostic measures of reliability of the computation and of similarity of the data sets being registered. At this point, the method presumes known correspondences, which is limiting, but the discussion in the end reveals some possibilities to overcome this issue, which we are examining. Practical properties are demonstrated on a typical task of localization of a robot with a known map.

articleTitle: Improvement of electricity end-consumer engagement in area of smart metering systems in Slovakia
abstract: The goal of this article is to provide an analysis of the implementation status of the obligations required from electricity market participants to provide measured data from smart metering devices to end-consumers through their web portal solutions. The data collected from smart metering system should provide electricity end-consumer with sufficient information about their consumption and/or generation. Such information has to cover sufficient volume of data for making proper decisions with regard to electricity load/generation management activities. It should also bring financial and technical benefits not only for consumers but also for other market participants. Based on the mapping of the existing and forthcoming EU and Slovak legislation, the current state of implementation of these obligations to publish measured data, foreign best practice solutions, the authors sought an optimal way of implementing these obligations, especially from the perspective of electricity end-consumers benefits.
